Review by gabriel 13

Brooks was here.

There’s something truly devastating about that particular scene. The one where we find something that’s been completely lost, the soul of a man no longer recognizing his own body, his way of living. Hope no longer visible to the eye, the freedom that a cloistered human so long dreams of never materializes into anything that is of any true meaning to him due to the inability to adjust to new times, to a new life, after spending so many years living in a certain way. It’s heart shattering.

For all its hopeful and hopeless moments and the dialogue that makes us think about life and how we perceive it and other people as well, this is an incredibly touching and emotional piece of cinema, one I should've watched ages ago.

Review by Mike Flanagan 47

Rang in the new year rewatching this with my 15 year-old son (his first time seeing it), and my father, who is visiting for the holidays. A perfect film, and a perfect evening, with three generations of my family appreciating this timeless story of friendship, endurance, and hope. My father was 45 when it came out, two years younger than I am now. I was 16 when it came out, only a year older than my son is now. I wonder who he'll be the next time he revisits it.
